---
title: "Pipes and method chains"
---

A table function such as `filter(...)` returns a closure that takes a table.
The PHP 8.5 pipe operator `|>`, `pipe()`, and a method chain started with
`phplyr()` apply such closures in order and give the same result.
[Pipelines](../getting-started.qmd#pipelines) shows the three forms.

## Pipelines

{{< include _api/chains-pipelines.md >}}

## Chain methods

`phplyr($table)` returns a `Phplyr\Chain`. Each table function runs as the
chain method of the same name in camelCase, such as `->groupBy()` for
`group_by()`; [Functions and methods](index.qmd) lists them. A method whose
function returns a table returns a new chain, and any other result is returned
as it is. A snake_case method name throws `BadMethodCallException` naming the
camelCase method.

### `->get()` {#chain-get}

```php
$chain->get(): Table
```

Returns the chain's table.

### `->pipe()` {#chain-pipe}

```php
$chain->pipe(callable ...$steps): mixed
```

Applies each step to the table in order. Returns a new chain when the result
is a table, and the result itself otherwise.

### `echo` {#chain-echo}

```php
echo $chain;
```

Prints the table, as `echo $table` does.
